newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures drift, gas oil up in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures drift, gas oil up in quiet trade.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures traded quietly on Wednesday, awaiting New York's opening to give the markets some direction, brokers said.

April gas oil, which settled at $165.50 a tonne on Tuesday, defied predictions it would trade $1.00 lower by opening narrowly down before gaining $1.25 to $166.75 by 1023 GMT. Dealers said there was nothing substantial behind the rise.
"There is nothing in particular driving it and it could just as easily come off," said one.
May Brent initially slipped below $19 before recovering to $19.07 a barrel by 1026 GMT.

May fell to $18.96, off 15 cents from yesterday's settlement as it caught up with U.S. losses posted in anticipation of bearish weekly stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), before retracing its steps.
"There's no real volume at the moment and no reaction to the APIs," said a trader, "There's no real news out as such, we're just waiting for NYMEX to open to give us a lead."
One broker said a a spate of diesel buying by one Singapore trader, triggering what may be the largest ever flow of diesel from West to East, could have been a factor in gas oil's strength.
Others saw gas oil supported by Brent.
